why: Item 13 mixes attack alarms and defence with watching and fixing, so the line between fighting an attack and routine repair is hard to hold.

why.T3-009: The dominant material is pride, congratulations, and marking the SG/BM murals as achieved.
why.T3-043: It also explicitly credits designers, builders, defenders and the starter, which T3-009's celebration gate does not carry.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: T3-009 carries the celebration and pride but not the explicit thanks and credit to the designers, starter and contributors.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: C1105614 credits designers/builders/defenders, C0245579 thanks the starter, and C0274588 tells contributors they are the best, satisfying T3-043's credit gate.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: Drop T3-043; we would lose the credit/thanks strand to the people who made and defended the murals.

why.T3-117: It treats the closed event as something to hope returns, suggesting next April 1 rather than planning a specific later canvas.

why.T3-088: The only concept is using old alt accounts in different browsers to place more quickly, which is placing beyond the one-pixel limit.

why.T3-038: The concepts announce stages completed and the next job (cleanup, defence, another logo), i.e. building progress rather than celebration of the whole finished work.

why.T3-004: Most concepts settle the SG mark's look: size, pixel art, ideas, simplicity, embellishments, and tweaks.
why.T3-038: Other concepts actually start or build the small and proper SG logo beneath the banner.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: T3-004 carries the design decisions but not the actual starts of the banner/logo placement.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: C0820510, C0116720 and C0341530 report making or starting the SG mark, satisfying T3-038's building gate.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: Drop T3-038; we would lose the fact that the mark was actually being built, not just designed.

why.T3-105: The item preserves the finished mural through full and cropped timelapses and thanks the person who made the enlarged view, matching saving screenshots/timelapses.

why.T3-073: The concepts recount what happened to the work: improvised start, fear of damaging it, destruction/reformation, Spica's origin, and checkerboard battles, not grief or celebration.

why.T3-024: The room repeatedly chooses to spare or work around neighbours' art (SRT, snek tongue, adjacent image) to avoid erasing others' work.

why.T3-127: The concepts ask to show the finished SG canvas work to SG staff and encourage doing so, seeking the creators'/staff's notice.

why.T3-040: The room apologises for drawing over a neighbour's character and offers pixels to redraw it nearby.
why.T3-170: The suspected throwaway blockers are identified as attempted helpers, and the room offers to stop—mistaken help recognised and forgiven.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: T3-040 carries the apology and repair for overwriting a neighbour, but not the recognition that apparent blockers were actually friendly helpers.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: C0934604 and C0431033 show throwaway accounts suspected of blocking being identified as attempted helpers who offer to stop, satisfying T3-170.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: Drop T3-170; we would lose the mistaken-help strand inside the SG logo.

why.T3-105: The item preserves the finished mural through full and cropped timelapses and thanks the person who made the enlarged view, matching saving screenshots/timelapses.

why.T3-002: The item calls r/mariokart members and visitors to send help/reinforcements to keep Pixel Mario Kart in shape, fitting a call for hands to place.

why.T3-005: The item is dominated by attack alarms, calls for help, reporting assaults, and rallying defenders around the SG/BM murals, so it is defence against attackers rather than routine repair.

why.T3-054: The concepts restart or offer a later canvas (pxls.space clone) after closure, which is carrying the work to new canvases rather than merely marking the end.

why.T3-001: The Daily is replaced by a staged April Fools joke post and commenters play along with invented show details, matching the room's own April Fools fake and replies inside it.
